business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Supply of Drummed and Bagged Penetration Grade Bitumen

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (entered into force 1991)
Panama-Republic of Korea Double Taxation Agreement (2009)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 2015 (AML/CFT) as amended by Law 70 of 2019; Executive Decree 363 of 2015; Law 25 of 1995 (Private Interest Foundations); SUI (Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros) resolutions on beneficial ownership registration.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación / Escritura Pública)
Certificate of Legal Entity Existence (Certificado de Persona Jurídica)
Resident Agent Appointment and Acceptance Letter

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against PEPs (domestic and foreign), OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU and domestic Panamanian SUI watchlists. Enhanced due diligence required for any PEP, adverse media, or high-risk source of funds; ongoing continuous screening at least annually and upon significant events.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá) – Online Name Reservation and Verification System (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be in Spanish or any language using the Latin alphabet; non-Latin scripts require a verified transliteration into Latin characters. The name must include the mandatory suffix 'Private Interest Foundation' or 'Fundación de Interés Privado' (or accepted abbreviation 'PIF') and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written 'Recurso de Reconsideración' before the Dirección General del Registro Público within 15 calendar days of notification. If denied, a 'Recurso de Apelación' may be lodged with the Corte Suprema de Justicia pursuant to administrative procedure. The applicant may simultaneously submit a revised name reservation for a new 30-day period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Purported virtual-only offices are not acceptable; a physical office within Panama maintained by the resident agent is mandatory. A rented serviced office located at the resident agent's licensed premises is permissible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a low-risk standard wholesale entity; estimated annualized on-site inspection probability below 10% absent adverse indicators such as PEP status, sanctions flags, or inconsistent commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Law 12 of 20 April 2017, Articles 4, 6, 9, 13, 18, 19 and 20; Executive Decree No. 20 of 12 July 2017 on registration implementation of foundations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Foundations of Private Interest Section, Mercantile Division, Via Simón Bolívar, Panama City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Private Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación de Interés Privado), executed as a notarial deed before a Notary Public of the First Circuit of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum initial endowment of US$10,000 pursuant to Law 25, Article 6, contributable in cash, securities, or assets and stated in the Foundation Charter; no mandatory bank escrow account is required at formation, but the founder must assign the endowment to the foundation patrimony prior to or upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned Founder and the Foundation Council hereby accept the transfer and contribution of the initial endowment capital of US$10,000, which shall constitute the foundation's patrimony. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Foundation be established at the address recorded in the Foundation Charter, Panama City, with the Resident Agent at said address pursuant to Law 25 of 1995. RESOLVED, that the named individuals be appointed President, Secretary, and Treasurer of the Foundation Council, each vested with full authority to open bank accounts, execute documents, and manage the foundation's affairs. RESOLVED, that the Council adopt the Foundation Regulations attached as Schedule A and authorize the Resident Agent to complete all statutory registrations, pay official fees, and obtain the certificate of registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the First Circuit of Panama (Notaría Pública del Primer Circuito de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed local attorney and resident agent; define the foundation name (to include 'Fundación de Interés Privado'), the initial endowment of at least US$10,000, the foundation's object, the Council members, beneficiaries, and protector if any; execute the Acta de Fundación before the notary, who certifies the legal capacity of the founder(s) and the conformity of the deed with Law 25 of 1995.
required_dossiers: Draft Foundation Charter
Founder's passport or identity document
Endowment contribution statement
Draft Foundation Regulations (optional at execution)
Power of attorney in favor of the resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries or rejects the deed, correct the deficient clauses (e.g., object, capital, or name), re-execute the instrument before the same notary, and obtain a new certified first copy; resubmission is typically completed the same business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Official State Registration Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá and Public Registry of Panama Cashier (Recaudaría del Registro Público)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the registry fee assessment form based on the declared foundation capital; deposit US$250 (or the amount assessed) at Banco Nacional de Panamá using the official registry deposit slip or pay electronically via the registry collection portal; retain the stamped deposit voucher as proof of payment for submission with the charter.
required_dossiers: Registry fee assessment form
Bank deposit voucher (ficha de depósito BNP)
Copy of the notarized Foundation Charter
Identity document of the submitting attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the payment is misapplied or lost, present the stamped voucher to the Registry's treasury section (Rectoría) to obtain a credit memo and reallocation of funds to the foundation file; issuance of the corrected receipt takes one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Registration with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama, Foundations of Private Interest Section (Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Foundation Charter, the fee voucher, and the resident agent's power of attorney to the Foundations Section; the Registry examines the deed for compliance with Law 25 (name, endowment, object, council, protector, and regulations) and inscribes the foundation in the register; the express for-fee service allows priority review within 48 hours if a faster turnaround is required.
required_dossiers: Certified first copy of the notarized Foundation Charter
Stamped Banco Nacional deposit voucher
Power of attorney of the resident agent
Negative registration certificate (certificado de no conflicto de nombre), where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect note (nota de defecto), remedy the stated omissions within the statutory term (usually 30 days), re-file the corrected deed, and pay any applicable re-submission fee; an expedited re-review can be requested with legal justification if a transaction deadline depends on the registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Certificate of Legal Existence and Tax Identification (RUC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (certificate issuance) and General Directorate of Revenue (Dirección General de Ingresos, DGI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the certified Certificate of Foundation Registration (Certificado de Personería Jurídica) from the Registry; thereafter apply to the DGI for the foundation's taxpayer registration number (RUC) using the standard taxpayer registration form; if physical office or warehouse premises are opened in Panama, file the municipal business notice (Aviso de Operación) with the corresponding Alcaldía; request a legal certification listing the Council members for banking purposes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Foundation Registration
Registered copy of the Foundation Charter
DGI taxpayer registration form (Form 971)
Passports of Council members and resident agent
Lease agreement or domiciliation certificate for the registered office (if premises are maintained)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI delays RUC issuance, escalate through the DGI taxpayer services office with a written follow-up and evidence of the registered foundation; if the municipality queries the Aviso de Operación, present the notarized lease and the certified Registry certificate to the municipal treasury to cure the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Foundation Regulations and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council (Consejo de la Fundación), Resident Agent, and the Apostille Office of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Dirección de Apostilla de la Cancillería)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the notarized First Board Resolution accepting the endowment, confirming the registered office address, and appointing the officers of the Foundation Council; adopt the private Foundation Regulations (Reglamento) signed by all council members; the Resident Agent records both documents in the foundation's minute book; where foreign banks require it, procure an apostille on the resolution and on the Foundation Charter for use in Swift LC and TT Wire account openings.
required_dossiers: Draft First Board Resolution
Draft Foundation Regulations
Certified Certificate of Registration
Passports of the signed Council members
Notarized power of attorney of the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification, verify that all Council members present have signed the original resolution and attach a certified copy of the registered charter; if apostille delivery is delayed, use the express apostille channel of the Cancillería to reduce processing to one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking and Commercial Readiness Pack for Swift LC and TT Wire Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panama universal private banks, supervised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the standard corporate package for opening the foundation's operating account: certified copy of the registered charter, apostilled First Board Resolution, Council members' identification, and the registered office domiciliation certificate; file the beneficial ownership declaration with the bank's AML compliance officer as required by Decree No. 23 of 2018; provide the business description evidencing wholesale trading of containerized penetration grade bitumen to justify the anticipated Swift LC and TT Wire transaction flows.
required_dossiers: Apostilled Foundation Charter and First Board Resolution
Certificate of Foundation Registration
AML and beneficial ownership declaration forms (beneficiario final registry filing receipt)
Business profile for bitumen wholesale (ISIC 4661 / NAICS 424720)
Proof of registered office and Resident Agent appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects or conditions the account opening, file or complete the beneficial ownership registration in the DGI Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales), obtain the official receipt, and resubmit the entire package through the bank's compliance committee; engage senior banking counsel to clarify any enhanced due diligence queries, emphasizing the low-risk standard wholesale trading classification and the absence of manufacturing exposure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce and Industries of Panama (Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias, MICI) for commercial licensing, and the Municipal Government (Alcaldía) of the premises' district for the business operation notice.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Business Operation Notice) for permanent registered premises; a MICI commercial license is only required if the foundation operates a physical sales office or warehouse in Panama. Containerized and drummed bitumen wholesale trading does not require an industrial manufacturing permit, as the activity is classified as trading and logistics, not processing or refining.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Panama (Ministerio de Ambiente, MiAMBIENTE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 0 Regime — registration only; exempt from a full Environmental Impact Study for pure trading, storage, and distribution of packaged (drummed) bitumen without hot-mix, refining, or heating operations. If a permanent warehouse above 500 m2 is leased, a simple Environmental Operation Registration (Registro de Operación) with MiAMBIENTE must be filed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Any leased warehouse must comply with the CECAS norm for wastewater discharges (Resolución AG-0688-2014): pH between 6 and 9, BOD5 not exceeding 100 mg/L, and TSS not exceeding 100 mg/L; no fugitive VOC combustion or open burning of bitumen residues is permitted; saturated rags, residual drums, and asphalt waste must be managed under Law 8 of 2018 (Basura Cero) and MiAMBIENTE dangerous waste protocols; containerized goods must remain sealed during transport to prevent vapor release and contamination of port or storage premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: SINAPROC Fire Safety Certificate (Certificado Técnico de Prevención de Incendios) is required for any leased warehouse storing packaged bitumen; a structural load inspection certificate issued by a licensed Panamanian engineer is required for the storage area; if employees are hired, an occupational health and safety program and clearance from the Ministry of Labor (MITRADEL) must be registered; the administrative registered office requires only a notarized domiciliation certificate issued by the Resident Agent.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama; electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must appoint a resident agent in Panama, execute public deed of incorporation or foundation charter before a Panamanian notary, obtain a Certified Public Registry filing, then apply for an RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) via the DGI Sede Electrónica. The RUC application requires statutory foundation deed, proof of resident agent, registration certificate from the Public Registry, and identification of directors, resident representative, and economic activity. The Panamanian RUC is the single statutory tax ID used for ITBMS, income tax, and customs purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box classification election exists in Panama. Entity tax status is determined by territorial source rules: only Panamanian-source income is subject to Panamanian income tax; foreign-source income earned by a Private Interest Foundation is generally exempt. A PIF may elect to register with DGI for VAT/ITBMS purposes if engaging in taxable activities in Panama, and may elect the simplified small-taxpayer ITBMS regime if annual gross income does not exceed B/.36,000. No hybrid mismatch elections are available under Panamanian domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) — Panamanian Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis registration threshold for ITBMS. Any person engaged in taxable activities in Panama (including sale of movable goods, rendering services, and imports) must register for ITBMS. A simplified regime (Régimen Simplificado de Tributación) is available for small taxpayers with annual gross income up to B/.36,000, but registration under that regime is optional; exporters must register under the general regime to claim zero-rating and refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing through the DGI's Facturación Electrónica de Panamá (FEP) platform. The DGI operates a real-time fiscal clearance system via API: taxpayers must submit invoice data to the DGI Authorization Service (Servicio de Autorización de la DGI) to obtain a digital stamp (código de verificación) and unique invoice code before issuance. Taxpayers must use authorized electronic invoicing software or the free DGI web application. Mandatory use of the digital stamp, QR code, and automated reporting to the DGI is required for ITBMS-registered entities; phased enrollment applies by taxpayer category.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and internationally rendered services are subject to ITBMS at 0%. To qualify, the taxpayer must provide documentary evidence that the goods or services left Panamanian territory and were provided to a foreign recipient. Export sales must be invoiced to a non-Panamanian customer, and payment must generally be received from abroad, unless an express DGI authorization covers exceptional local payment arrangements. The zero-rated supply must be clearly identified in the electronic invoice as an export transaction and reported in the ITBMS periodic return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Declaración Única Aduanera) duly endorsed by the National Customs Authority
Bill of Lading or waybill showing physical departure of goods from Panamanian territory
Commercial invoice issued by the exporter to the foreign buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer evidence proving payment received from abroad (where applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating claims trigger retrospective ITBMS assessment on the full invoice amount, plus statutory interest from the original due date. Administrative penalties include fines of up to 200% of the omitted tax where false documentation is used, and criminal sanctions under Panama's Fiscal Criminal Law (Ley 14 de 2013) for tax fraud carry imprisonment penalties of 3 to 6 years and disqualification from holding public or commercial offices. Zero-rating benefits may be retroactively clawed back for a period of up to five years, and the exporter may lose the right to apply for refunds for a defined period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama does not operate a conventional central bank or monetary authority. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (Superintendency of Banks of Panama, SBP) is the primary prudential supervisor of the Panama Banking Center; the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) serves as the national Financial Intelligence Unit; the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) and the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) administer fiscal policy. Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as a state-owned commercial bank and fiscal agent rather than a lender of last resort. The US Dollar (USD) is legal tender and circulates alongside the Panamanian Balboa (PAB), which exists only as token coins pegged at 1:1 to the USD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Currency convertibility is effectively absolute under the dollarized regime: there is no Panamanian central bank FX market, no exchange control, and no restriction on current-account or capital-account flows. Treasury operations are conducted 100% in USD, eliminating conversion friction for bitumen trade settlements. Capital account: PIF endowments, subsequent capital injections, distributions, and loan repayments are unrestricted for non-resident owners; profit remittance is free where income is foreign-source under Panama's territorial tax system. The only practical constraints are correspondent-banking compliance: originating and receiving banks must verify legal origin of funds, pass OFAC/UAF sanction screening, and accept the PIF's beneficial-ownership documentation; banks may independently decline transfers to or from high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Panama imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender regime, no mandatory conversion ratio, no repatriation timeline, and no export receipt polling requirement. USD-denominated bitumen receipts may be retained offshore, deposited into the PIF's Panamanian account, or cleared through the Zona Libre de Colón banking channels without conversion or central bank approval. Because the PIF's wholesale bitumen income derived from foreign counterparties originates outside Panama for territorial tax purposes, receipt of such proceeds does not of itself create Panamanian taxable income or trigger any clearance obligation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for auxiliary collection rails only; Low for primary treasury. Panama has no EU-style EMI licence; the SBP-authorized 'Sociedades de Pago' regime permits approved payment-service firms to maintain payment accounts, but these are domestically oriented and rarely support LC or trade flows. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) frequently decline Panamanian PIFs due to perceived beneficial-ownership opacity and the inability of EMI rails to execute SWIFT MT700 letters of credit. Legal constraint: an offshore EMI cannot issue commercial LCs, cannot access the Panama Banking Center domestic clearing, and cannot satisfy local RUC-linked banking evidence. Strategic verdict: use EMIs solely for pre-warehousing of small deposits below USD 50,000; the principal treasury, LC desk, and FX lines must sit with an SBP-licensed Tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in substance. SBP Rule 01-2012 and Law 23 of 2015 require verification of the founder, all Foundation Council members, the protector (if any), and the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) before account activation. Purely remote onboarding for a non-resident PIF is not a standard market practice; most Tier-1 banks require at least one Principal or an appointed legal representative with Senior Vice President authority to attend a face-to-face onboarding interview in Panama City. The UBO should appear in person; alternatively, the bank may accept a notarized and apostilled power of attorney supplemented by a remote video confirmation at the bank's discretion. Budget for a dedicated 2- to 3-day visit, including execution of the foundation operating resolution and specimen signature cards.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF legal structure perceived as opaque: 'Foundation' name, historic bearer-participation connotations, and multi-layer council/protector governance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Pacto Fundacional (Private Interest Foundation charter) with notarial and apostille stamps; sworn statement from the Foundation Council identifying the founder, council members, protector, and UBO; organizational chart showing control chain; written declaration that any bearer participation has been immobilized or cancelled in compliance with Law 23 of 2015; current registration certificate from the Public Registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity for the initial endowment and for high-value bitumen trade flows routed from multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete commercial chain documentation: endorsed bills of lading, commercial invoices, product quality certificates, refinery supplier master purchase agreements, end-customer purchase orders, pre-shipment inspection certificates, plus bank reference letters from the counterparties' banks; cash-flow forecast linked to the bitumen working-capital cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large lump-sum inbound capital injection versus modest running balance, which may trigger unusual-activity profiling for a private interest foundation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundation Council resolution authorizing the capital injection and the target operating corridor (e.g., USD 200,000 to USD 1,500,000); notarized funding statement (declaración de aportación); source-of-funds statement from the settlor's existing bank; budget and treasury policy evidencing intended deployment toward containerized bitumen procurement and freight.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party mandate authority of the local resident agent and remote disbursement instructions creating red flags for potential misappropriation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Limited mandate letter expressly restricting the resident agent's authority; dual-signature and two-man rule for all disbursements; designated council members with specimen signatures certified before the bank; sworn undertaking that settlor rights and PIF governance are properly recorded in the Special Registry as required for Private Interest Foundations under Panamanian law.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing is via SWIFT MT103 from a pre-identified depositor bank, using SWIFT/ISO 20022 purpose codes 'COST' (capital) or 'CAPT' (capital contribution) for the foundation endowment and 'GF01' or 'GF00' for general investment flows; the remittance information field must contain the PIF's Panamanian Tax ID (RUC) and foundation registration number. Because Panama has no exchange control, no central bank authorization is required; however, the receiving bank will demand (i) the Foundation Council resolution approving the capital injection, (ii) a notarized aportación/funding statement, (iii) the sending bank's source-of-funds reference, and (iv) a one-paragraph transaction rationale tied to the bitumen procurement cycle. Amounts above USD 1,000,000 warrant a pre-funding consultation with the bank's compliance desk to avoid inbound wire holds. Immediately following first funding, dual-control disbursement governance should be activated and bank forwarding instructions re-verified by SWIFT or MT199 to prevent fraud.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Three-tier clearing strategy for containerized bitumen wholesaling: (1) SWIFT MT103 for operational payments (container handling, stevedoring, freight, terminal fees, inspection and agency commissions) within standing-instruction limits; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit via MT700/MT720 for refinery supplier settlements, supplemented by MT760 standby LCs for performance bonds and advance-payment guarantees to emulsion plants; (3) Documentary collections (MT400 series) for repeat open-account-friendly counterparties. All outbound instructions must clear the bank's UAF/OFAC-screened counterparty database and conform to INCOTERMS 2020 (CIF or CFR) matched to the bill of lading, commercial invoice, certificate of quality, and marine insurance certificate. For Chinese or Northern South American refinery supply chains, ensure the LC is irrevocable, confirmed (if requested), and payable at sight; the PIF should hold board-approved LC templates and a renewal calendar.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR and USD/CNH deliverable forwards with SBP-licensed banks, used to hedge non-USD supplier invoices or European customer collections in the bitumen supply chain
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on USD/CNH and select Latin American currencies where physical delivery is impeded, executed with the bank's offshore treasury desk
Cross-currency swaps for structural matching of EUR receivables from EU buyers against USD/CNH payables to refineries and container logistics providers
Natural hedging via multi-currency account sets (USD, EUR, CNH custody positions) maintained at the Tier-1 bank, with periodic rebalancing to limit FX risk since the PIF's functional currency is USD

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Tax / State Franchise Fee (Impuesto Anual de Fundación)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance; payment evidenced to the Registro Público de Panamá for continuity of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 31 March; no anniversary-based prorating
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% of the annual tax plus annualized interest; prolonged failure to pay for two consecutive periods subjects the Foundation to administrative suspension and strike-off from the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta) — applicable only when the PIF generates Panamanian-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of the calendar year following each fiscal year; the fiscal year ends 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 10% on the tax due, monthly administrative interest under the Tax Code, and possible registry/authorization obstacles for non-filing; deliberate non-compliance may escalate to criminal tax penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panamanian registered agent; UBO data maintained in the Foundation's private registry and registered in the Registro de Beneficiario Final system when legally required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year, typically within 30 days after the Foundation's registration anniversary, and within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Panama AML Law (Law 23 of 2015) against the Foundation or its agent; possible registry suspension for non-compliance with AML measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual Renewal / Acceptance of Continued Role
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panamanian registered agent under contract (licensed attorney or resident agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewed on each registration anniversary according to the registered-agent services agreement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Agent may resign; failure to maintain a licensed resident agent results in registry suspension and, if uncured, administrative strike-off of the Foundation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit applies under Law 25 of 1995 solely because the entity is a Private Interest Foundation. A mandatory independent audit could arise only if the Foundation becomes subject to a Panamanian DGI requirement triggered by Panamanian-source business activity above the prescribed financial-statement threshold, or if the Foundation's statutory deed deliberately imposes an audit. For the ordinary PIF holding bitumen-derivative trading and logistics contracts, no audit mandate is triggered by the absence of Panamanian-source revenue.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama (NIIF) or IFRS for SMEs; Foundation accounting records must be kept sufficient to determine assets, liabilities and operations, and to support annual franchise-tax compliance and any Panamanian-source income tax declaration.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The PIF's registered agent must annually obtain a written declaration from the foundation council confirming the ultimate beneficial owners, protector, and any holders of foundation certificates; any transfer of an economic interest in the Foundation is documented by amending the private foundation deed or certificate and filing a new UBO confirmation with the registered agent within 30 days. The agent keeps this information confidential but accessible for inspection by the Panamanian Financial Analysis Unit and DGI under Law 23 of 2015; no public annual shareholding filing is made for PIFs.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Interests / Economic Rights

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $900 – $1,500 per annum for a Panamanian licensed corporate agent and registered address
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not mandatory for the PIF; market estimate $4,500 – $9,000 if an independent CPA audit is voluntarily commissioned or required by the DGI.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat corporate income tax (ISR) under Law 8 of 2010. A preferential graduated scale applies only when annual taxable income does not exceed USD 1,500,000: 15% on the first USD 50,000 and 25% on the band between USD 50,001 and USD 1,500,000. Where taxable income exceeds USD 1,500,000, the entire amount is taxed at 25%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial source rule: ISR attaches only to Panamanian-source income. Profit on the containerized wholesale supply of penetration-grade bitumen (ISIC 4661 / NAICS 424720), where title, risk, transport and delivery are executed outside Panama, is foreign-source and carries a 0% effective rate. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF, Ley 25 de 1995) is a non-commercial vehicle; its endowment and distributions are not subjects of ISR. Special regimes further compress the effective rate: SEM Multinational Headquarters (Ley 41 de 2007) 0% on qualifying foreign services, Panama Pacifico SEZ exemptions and a 5% dividend withholding credit on taxed profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (Declaración Anual de Renta) filed through the DGI e-filing portal (Dirección General de Ingresos en línea — www.dgi.gob.pa / dgi.mef.gob.pa). Transfer pricing taxpayers attach Form 124 (Declaración Informativa de Precios de Transferencia) to the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Quarterly advance ISR instalments (pagos fraccionados) are due during the 4th, 6th, 9th and 12th months of the fiscal year by taxpayers whose prior-year gross revenue exceeded USD 300,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Calendar-year taxpayers must file Form 100 on or before 15 March of the year following the fiscal year-end; non-calendar fiscal periods must file within three months of the fiscal year-end. DGI may stagger the exact file-by date by the last digit of the RUC, but 15 March is the operative statutory anchor for 31 December year-ends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total invoiced revenue. This line is the screening point for the territorial test; only revenue sourced in Panama is includible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Containerized bitumen sales completed with INCOTERM title transfer at a foreign port (FOB/CIF ex-Panama port) are excluded; attach a schedule detailing bill of lading and contract counterparty to support the exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 – Cost of sales (Costo de ventas)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct acquisition cost of drummed and bagged penetration-grade bitumen, freight, container demurrage and marine insurance allocable to Panamanian-source sales only.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Keep per-container cost sheets; costs allocated to foreign-source sales are removed to preserve territorial gross margin neutrality.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: registered-agent fees, foundation board costs, logistics oversight, port inspection, communications and legal expenses incurred in Panama and directly linked to taxable Panamanian-source activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses of the PIF must be in the foundation's name and evidenced by RUC-validated invoices; non-resident settlor travel and personal costs are non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 – Net taxable income (Renta neta gravable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Line 1 minus Lines 2 and 3. Where the taxpayer is a PIF with no Panamanian-source commercial income and no local trading activity, this line is reported as 0.00.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A zero figure must be coherent with zero withholdings and zero quarterly advances; an unexplained loss or zero against third-party shipping records is a DGI red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 5 – ISR due at 15%/25% (Impuesto sobre la renta)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the graduated scale only where taxable income is at or below USD 1,500,000; apply the flat 25% to all taxable income above that threshold. Credit any quarterly advances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No foreign tax credit is available for income exempt under the territorial rule; claiming credit for taxes paid abroad is a common fatal error.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare corporate-level ISR paid and compute the 5% dividend withholding tax on dividends actually paid or credited during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends remitted to the settlor or beneficiary of a PIF are subject to 5% if paid from taxed profits and 10% if paid from non-taxed offshore profits; remit via Swift LC or TT wire only after filing Form 100 and paying the WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7 – Transfer pricing annex (Anexo TP / Form 124)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose intercompany transactions with related suppliers of bitumen, freight forwarders and logistics operators above the statutory threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident related counterparties require a Panama TP local file narrative: CUP benchmark of comparable Ancap/Pemex/API grade bitumen prices, functions and risks analysis, and a TNMM fallback where no comparable exists.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a surcharge of 5% per month or fraction of the tax due, capped at 50% of the tax, plus 1% monthly interest on the outstanding ISR. Failure to file Form 100 absent tax liability triggers administrative fines of USD 100 to USD 5,000. Failure to pay quarterly advances attracts 10% annual interest and automatic summons (aviso de cobro). Wilful non-filing escalates to criminal fiscal evasion (see Red Flags).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% domestic withholding rate on dividends paid from profits that have borne Panamanian ISR (Law 8 of 2010). Dividends paid from profits that were not subject to Panama ISR—i.e., foreign-source trading profits under the territorial regime—are subject to a 10% dividend withholding tax. A PIF receiving dividends from a Panama operating entity is the taxable recipient and must see the WHT documented before repatriation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: DTA relief is not granted automatically. Before each dividend, interest or royalty payment the non-resident recipient must: (i) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the applicable treaty partner tax authority, apostilled and translated where required; (ii) provide the Panama payer with a beneficial-ownership statement on the DGI prescribed form; (iii) file the DGI treaty rate application at least 15 business days before payment. The Panama payer may then withhold at the reduced DTA rate (commonly 5%–10% dividends, 0%–10% interest, 5%–10% royalties). Over-withheld tax is recoverable via the DGI refund procedure within three years of the payment date.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic rates: royalties and technical/management fees paid to non-residents are subject to 12.5% gross Panama withholding if paid for the use of IP or technical assistance in Panama; interest paid to non-resident lenders on genuine trade credit is statutorily exempt (0%) where the lender carries on no business in Panama and the loan is registered, while other interest can attract 6%. Treaty rates under Panama's DTA network generally cap interest at 10% (0% for some government/bank debt) and royalties at 5%–10%, provided the protocol described above is completed.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 3,000,000 in annual gross revenue triggers the transfer-pricing documentation duty, with mandatory Form 124 filing when related-party transactions exceed USD 1,000,000 in a year. A Master File obligation arises for multinational groups with consolidated revenue above USD 50,000,000. Lower-threshold taxpayers must still prepare contemporaneous CUP/TNMM calculations upon DGI audit request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations statute; ESR is operationalized through the territorial nexus doctrine, the 2016 transfer-pricing regime (Executive Decree 530), CRS/FATCA registration duties, and the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework commitment. A PIF and its bitumen trading subsidiary are required to evidence: (1) a Panamanian registered office and registered agent; (2) foundation council resolutions directing each containerized trade; (3) segregated books and records located physically in Panama; and (4) paid, locally resident staff making logistics contracting decisions. A purely passive nominee structure is re-characterized by DGI as an agent or sham: the foreign-source profit is stripped of its exemption and assessed at 25%.
